residual_findings.title: Intermittent flaky test `fallback_warn_includes_chapter_field` (review_report) fails under full parallel `cargo test -p nexus-orchestration`; passes in isolation. Pre-existing on iteration/v1.49 base.
residual_findings.source: P1 implementer (pre-existing flake, verified against base per .mstar/AGENTS.md protocol); QC3 also verified on origin/main @ be27111b
residual_findings.note: Verified pre-existing per the repo's 'Pre-existing claim verification protocol': reproduces on iteration/v1.49 @ 3630a4e5 (base) with `cargo test -p nexus-orchestration` (full parallel suite — 9 passed, 1 failed in review_report); passes with `cargo test -p nexus-orchestration --test review_report` (in isolation, parallel and serial). QC3 also verified on origin/main @ be27111b with 2/10 failure rate. Cause: global tracing registry contention when many test binaries install/inspect the subscriber concurrently. Not caused by V1.49 P1 — review_report.rs and its capture layer are untouched. Suggested fix: scoped subscriber guard or serializing that single test.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T1: marked every test in tests/review_report.rs with #[serial_test::serial] so the whole binary runs mutually exclusively (equivalent to --test-threads=1 for this binary; other binaries still parallelise). Diagnosis via eprintln probes confirmed the function fired its warn!/info! events on the calling thread with persisted_count=1 in both passing and failing runs — the capture layer was intermittently dropping the first event after install when sibling tests competed for the tokio blocking-thread pool that sqlx uses for SQLite I/O. Added serial_test = "3" to nexus-orchestration [dev-dependencies]. Verified 30/30 clean at --test-threads=8 (was ~3/30 failing), 5/5 at --test-threads=16, 5/5 cross-binary full suite. Also pinned the flaky test to #[tokio::test(flavor = "current_thread")] as defence-in-depth for the set_default guard's lifetime across .await.
